situation: A result looks impressive, but I’m not sure what it proves.

primary.description: Does the broader pattern support the explanation?

secondary.description: Is the summary hiding important differences?
Were expectations defined before seeing the results?

situation: I understand the findings, but I’m unsure what to do.

primary.description: Connect the evidence to a defensible recommendation.

situation: We keep gathering information without getting closer to a decision.

primary.description: Identify which unanswered question could actually change the choice.

situation: I’m unsure whether to act now or wait.

primary.description: Understand what waiting gains and costs.

secondary.description: See which future choices a commitment would close.
Find useful preparations that don't require committing yet.

situation: Something feels wrong, but I can’t explain why.

primary.description: Turn the concern into something you can examine.

secondary.description: Check whether the problem lies between different areas of expertise.

situation: A plan looks settled, but we may not agree on what it means.

primary.description: Identify assumptions being mistaken for commitments.

secondary.description: Reveal differences concealed by a shared description.

situation: Someone’s behavior doesn’t make sense to me.

primary.description: Question what you assume they are trying to achieve.

secondary.description: Avoid assuming more strategic intent than the evidence supports.

situation: The work looks good, but I don’t know whether it helped.

primary.description: Look beyond the quality of the work to its effects.
